title: Web App Security
summary: The vocabulary of defending web applications — OWASP Top 10, injection attacks, authentication and sessions, cross-site attacks, cryptography for developers, threat modeling, supply-chain security, SAST/DAST/SCA/IAST, AppSec in CI/CD, Zero Trust, and the 2026 LLM-augmented threat landscape.

volatileChapters.reason: LLM-augmented attack patterns evolve quarterly; new prompt-injection techniques + agent abuse vectors emerge continuously.

inspiredBy.title: OWASP + The Tangled Web + Threat Modeling (Shostack) + Real-World Cryptography (Wong)

chapters.title: The Web Security Mental Model
chapters.summary: Foundations — the same-origin policy, threat-actor model (script-kiddie, opportunistic, targeted, nation-state), defense in depth, principle of least privilege, and the security trade-off triangle.

chapters.title: OWASP Top 10
chapters.summary: The canonical web-app risk list — broken access control, cryptographic failures, injection, insecure design, security misconfiguration, vulnerable components, ID/auth failures, software/data integrity failures, logging failures, SSRF — with examples and mitigations.

chapters.title: Injection Attacks
chapters.summary: How untrusted input becomes code — SQL injection (classic, blind, time-based), NoSQL injection, command injection, LDAP injection, log injection, XPath/XML injection; defenses (parameterized queries, input validation, ORM safety).

chapters.title: Authentication and Sessions
chapters.summary: Identity on the web — password hashing (Argon2/bcrypt/scrypt), salting, peppering; OAuth 2.1, OIDC, JWT (and its pitfalls); session cookies vs tokens; MFA (TOTP, push, FIDO2); passkeys and WebAuthn; account-takeover defenses.

chapters.title: Cross-Site Attacks
chapters.summary: Browser-trust exploits — XSS (reflected/stored/DOM-based), CSRF, clickjacking, same-origin policy, CORS, Content Security Policy (CSP), SameSite cookies, Trusted Types, Subresource Integrity.

chapters.title: SSRF and IDOR
chapters.summary: Server-side and access-control bugs — Server-Side Request Forgery (basic + blind), cloud metadata theft (IMDSv1 vs v2), Insecure Direct Object Reference, mass assignment, broken access control patterns.

chapters.title: Cryptography for Developers
chapters.summary: What every dev needs — symmetric vs asymmetric, AEAD ciphers (AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305), hash functions, KDFs (PBKDF2, scrypt, Argon2), HMAC, TLS 1.3 fundamentals, certificate transparency, the do-not-roll-your-own rule.

chapters.title: Threat Modeling
chapters.summary: Designing for security — STRIDE, PASTA, attack trees, data flow diagrams, trust boundaries, threat-model-as-code (pytm), the four-questions framework (what / what could go wrong / what are we doing / did we do a good job).

chapters.title: Software Supply Chain Security
chapters.summary: Modern attack vectors — SBOM (CycloneDX, SPDX), SLSA framework levels, Sigstore + Cosign, provenance attestations, dependency confusion, typosquatting, malicious npm/PyPI packages, build attestations.

chapters.title: SAST / DAST / SCA / IAST
chapters.summary: Application security testing — Static Application Security Testing (Semgrep, Snyk Code, CodeQL), Dynamic (OWASP ZAP, Burp Suite), Software Composition Analysis (Snyk, Dependabot, Renovate), Interactive AST; how each tool fits the SDLC.

chapters.title: AppSec in CI/CD
chapters.summary: Security as a pipeline citizen — security gates, secret scanning (TruffleHog, gitleaks), IaC scanning (Checkov, tfsec), container scanning (Trivy, Grype), fuzz testing (OSS-Fuzz, libfuzzer), policy as code (OPA Rego).

chapters.title: Zero Trust Architecture
chapters.summary: Beyond the perimeter — BeyondCorp model, ZTA principles, identity-aware proxies (IAP, Cloudflare Access), service mesh mTLS, micro-segmentation, continuous verification, least-privilege identity.

chapters.title: Modern Threats in 2026
chapters.summary: The current attack landscape — LLM-assisted attacks (faster recon, polymorphic malware), prompt injection in agent systems, model exfiltration, AI-generated phishing, deepfake-driven social engineering, supply-chain attacks on AI models.
